purpose: Machine-readable routing index for selecting one runtime-visible Skill, one maintained workflow, or one material clarification.

modePolicy.direct: Select one highest-scoring runtime-visible Skill when it owns the complete requested result and has sufficient inputs.
modePolicy.workflow: Select one maintained workflow only when the request needs multiple independently accepted outputs or a real cross-Skill artifact dependency.
modePolicy.clarify: Ask one focused question only when the answer changes the selected Skill, workflow, or required input.

runtimeSemanticFallback.candidateContract: Score every plausible runtime-visible Skill against the complete intent card and select a maximum score; read the full Skill only for the winner or a genuine tie.
runtimeSemanticFallback.fallbackContract: If no indexed task class or preferred Skill covers the request, preserve the inferred inputs, constraints, deliverable, and acceptance contract, then discover and score runtime-visible Skills without inventing an ID.

taskClasses.label: Single creative output
taskClasses.useWhen: The request ends in one image, video, identity asset, or other independently usable creative result.
taskClasses.directWhen: One runtime-visible Atom owns the complete result, all material inputs are present, and no separate upstream artifact or research evidence is required.
taskClasses.orchestrateWhen: The result actually depends on a separately accepted source asset, research record, or multiple independently requested outputs.

taskClasses.label: Precision edit or restoration
taskClasses.useWhen: The user supplies media and asks for a bounded transformation while named content, identity, geometry, copy, or timing must be preserved.
taskClasses.directWhen: One edit Atom owns the requested change and the supplied source meets its input contract.
taskClasses.orchestrateWhen: The accepted edit must become a distinct input to a later layout, localization set, or post-production operation.

taskClasses.label: Commerce and fashion production
taskClasses.useWhen: The primary contract is product, garment, packaging, shopper communication, model styling, or buyer-decision content.
taskClasses.directWhen: A product or fashion Atom owns the complete requested asset or coherent set without a separately accepted upstream artifact.
taskClasses.orchestrateWhen: Product-faithful source creation feeds a separate page, campaign, channel, or multi-format deliverable.

taskClasses.label: Portrait and character identity
taskClasses.useWhen: The central invariant is a person, face, character, mascot, avatar, casting identity, or pet identity.
taskClasses.directWhen: One identity-owning Atom supplies the requested portrait, canonical sheet, avatar, or character result.
taskClasses.orchestrateWhen: A separately accepted canonical identity must be reused across pages, shots, poses, or a narrative sequence.

taskClasses.label: Layout, information design, and social series
taskClasses.useWhen: The outcome is a composed page, deck, poster, carousel, infographic, collage, or coordinated social set.
taskClasses.directWhen: One layout Atom owns the whole page or coherent series from the supplied content.
taskClasses.orchestrateWhen: Research, cutouts, translations, or separately produced hero media must be accepted and bound into later layouts or channel variants.

taskClasses.label: Narrative sequence
taskClasses.useWhen: The requested result has ordered story units whose continuity, identity, timing, or state carries across pages or shots.
taskClasses.directWhen: A specialized end-to-end Atom explicitly owns the complete sequence and no separate page, shot, manifest, or approval is requested.
taskClasses.orchestrateWhen: A story manifest, canonical identity, shot or page generation, and assembly are distinct artifact responsibilities.

taskClasses.label: Campaign or multi-deliverable bundle
taskClasses.useWhen: The user expects multiple independently usable channel assets, formats, or media types governed by one shared brief.
taskClasses.directWhen: A specialized Atom promises the exact coherent bundle as its single output contract, including all requested variants.
taskClasses.orchestrateWhen: Different Atoms own distinct deliverables or an accepted campaign source must feed parallel channel branches.

taskClasses.label: Post-production and finishing
taskClasses.useWhen: Existing media needs assembly, grading, repair, enhancement, mark removal, effects, or platform-ready finishing.
taskClasses.directWhen: One finishing Atom owns the complete requested transformation of the supplied media.
taskClasses.orchestrateWhen: Several accepted clips or localized assets must be processed in dependency order and delivered as a combined master plus variants.

taskClasses.label: Spatial and technical visualization
taskClasses.useWhen: The output communicates a room, landscape, floor plan, CAD object, process, evidence structure, or other geometry- or fact-sensitive system.
taskClasses.directWhen: One specialist Atom owns the complete visual or model and the source measurements or facts are already supplied.
taskClasses.orchestrateWhen: Current evidence or source measurements must first be verified and transformed into a separately accepted brief before visualization.

taskClasses.label: Prompt, planning, and diagnostics
taskClasses.useWhen: The requested deliverable is text: a prompt, screenplay, storyboard, adaptation, model recommendation, or failure diagnosis rather than generated media.
taskClasses.directWhen: One text Atom owns the exact requested document or diagnosis.
taskClasses.orchestrateWhen: Current research or multiple separately used planning artifacts have real downstream dependencies; requesting both a prompt and later generation alone does not split an Atom that owns both.

taskClasses.label: Skill and system management
taskClasses.useWhen: The user wants to create, revise, install, document, or maintain a Skill or system context rather than produce media.
taskClasses.directWhen: One management Skill owns the requested lifecycle result.
taskClasses.orchestrateWhen: Only when several management artifacts have actual dependencies; creative recipes must not be selected merely because the request discusses Skills.

tasks.label: Product-faithful commercial scene
tasks.useWhen: A supplied product must appear faithfully in one newly composed commercial environment or hero image.
tasks.directWhen: One accepted product scene is the complete result and no separate layout set or channel requirement must consume it.
tasks.escalateWhen: The accepted scene must feed a separately owned detail page, channel campaign, or researched marketplace deliverable.

tasks.label: White-background product mockup
tasks.useWhen: A supplied product needs one clean catalog-style white-background presentation with product geometry and labels preserved.
tasks.directWhen: The clean white-background asset is the final deliverable.
tasks.escalateWhen: The mockup is an accepted intermediate that must feed a separate detail-page or multi-format campaign deliverable.

tasks.label: Product detail-page set
tasks.useWhen: The result is a coherent modular page set that explains product value and supports a shopper decision.
tasks.directWhen: Supplied imagery and facts are sufficient and the Atom owns the complete requested page set.
tasks.escalateWhen: Current platform facts or a separately accepted product source must be created before the page set.

tasks.label: Product packaging design
tasks.useWhen: The requested result is a packaging concept or package-facing design for a supplied product and brand system.
tasks.directWhen: One packaging result is requested and all required copy and structural constraints are supplied.
tasks.escalateWhen: Packaging must be coordinated with separately produced identity, product imagery, or campaign formats.

tasks.label: Virtual garment try-on
tasks.useWhen: A specific garment must be placed on a supplied person while both garment and person identity remain central.
tasks.directWhen: One try-on result or ordinary batch is the complete output.
tasks.escalateWhen: Accepted try-on assets must feed separately owned lookbook, carousel, or multi-format campaign outputs. Seed a custom runtime DAG so the try-on owner remains an explicit upstream node.

tasks.label: Fashion model replacement
tasks.useWhen: A fashion image keeps the garment and composition while replacing the person wearing it.
tasks.directWhen: The model replacement itself is the final image result.
tasks.escalateWhen: The accepted replacement must be reused across a separately composed lookbook or campaign set. Seed a custom runtime DAG so the replacement owner remains an explicit upstream node.

tasks.label: Change a subject pose
tasks.useWhen: A supplied person or character must keep identity and appearance while adopting a different pose.
tasks.directWhen: The pose change is the only requested transformation.
tasks.escalateWhen: Multiple accepted poses become distinct inputs to a narrative, lookbook, or campaign workflow.

tasks.label: End-to-end product commercial
tasks.useWhen: The requested output is one complete commercial video centered on a product and shopper-facing proposition.
tasks.directWhen: The selected end-to-end Atom owns the complete video and no separate shot assets or channel branches are required.
tasks.escalateWhen: The user requires separately controlled shots, a reusable master plus channel assets, or explicit shot-level handoffs. Reclassify the final outcome as a narrative sequence or campaign bundle before choosing a recipe.

tasks.label: Logo design
tasks.useWhen: The complete result is a new logo mark or wordmark for a named identity and brief.
tasks.directWhen: One logo result or ordinary logo variation set is the complete deliverable.
tasks.escalateWhen: An accepted logo becomes a fixed input to several separately owned campaign formats. Seed a custom runtime DAG so logo creation remains an explicit upstream node.

tasks.label: Campaign banner design
tasks.useWhen: The result is a banner with a placement-specific hierarchy, supplied message, and campaign visual direction.
tasks.directWhen: Banner exports are the complete requested result.
tasks.escalateWhen: The banner is one branch of a campaign that also requires independently usable social, deck, or video outputs.

tasks.label: Poster design
tasks.useWhen: The outcome is one composed poster whose hierarchy, imagery, and exact copy form the complete result.
tasks.directWhen: The poster Atom can own the complete composition from the supplied material.
tasks.escalateWhen: A separately accepted cutout, research brief, or localized asset set must feed the poster.

tasks.label: Social carousel
tasks.useWhen: The requested result is a coherent ordered social carousel with a shared narrative and visual system.
tasks.directWhen: The carousel is the complete coherent series and all content inputs are supplied.
tasks.escalateWhen: Research, localized artwork, or separately generated hero media must be accepted before carousel composition.

tasks.label: Image deck
tasks.useWhen: The final result is a multi-page image deck organized for explanation, presentation, or distribution.
tasks.directWhen: The supplied evidence and content are sufficient for the deck Atom to own the complete result.
tasks.escalateWhen: Current facts must be researched and cited before the deck is composed.

tasks.label: Social or video thumbnail
tasks.useWhen: The complete result is a small-format click-oriented thumbnail for a supplied topic, subject, or source image.
tasks.directWhen: One thumbnail or ordinary variation batch is requested.
tasks.escalateWhen: The thumbnail is one separately owned branch of a wider campaign system. Use the campaign-bundle class so the requested branch set determines the recipe.

tasks.label: Information graphic
tasks.useWhen: Facts, comparisons, steps, or quantities must become one readable information-first visual.
tasks.directWhen: The user supplies sufficient authoritative content and one infographic is the final result.
tasks.escalateWhen: Current external facts materially determine the visual and require a verified evidence record first.

tasks.label: Translate copy inside artwork
tasks.useWhen: Text inside supplied artwork must change language while declared imagery, brand elements, and layout relationships remain preserved.
tasks.directWhen: One source image and one target locale form the complete request.
tasks.escalateWhen: Several sources, locales, or composed channel sets require a shared localization matrix and delivery manifest.

tasks.label: Remove image background
tasks.useWhen: A supplied foreground subject or product must be isolated on transparency with its boundary preserved.
tasks.directWhen: The transparent cutout is the final deliverable.
tasks.escalateWhen: The accepted cutout becomes a distinct input to a poster, banner, carousel, or detail layout.

tasks.label: Expand an image canvas
tasks.useWhen: An accepted image needs a larger canvas or different aspect ratio while its existing content remains intact.
tasks.directWhen: Aspect or canvas expansion is the only failed or requested property.
tasks.escalateWhen: The expanded image is a separately accepted source for a later independently owned composition.

tasks.label: Remove an object from an image
tasks.useWhen: One named object must be removed from supplied imagery while surrounding content remains coherent.
tasks.directWhen: Object removal is the complete bounded transformation.
tasks.escalateWhen: The repaired asset must feed a separately owned composition or multi-asset series.

tasks.label: Combine source images
tasks.useWhen: Several supplied images must be merged into one coherent image while their requested roles remain explicit.
tasks.directWhen: The merged image is the complete requested result.
tasks.escalateWhen: The merged asset becomes one accepted intermediate for a separately owned layout or campaign branch.

tasks.label: Create a canonical character
tasks.useWhen: A recurring original character needs one canonical design result that can anchor later scenes or pages.
tasks.directWhen: The canonical character result itself is the complete request.
tasks.escalateWhen: The accepted identity must feed multiple comic pages or narrative shots.

tasks.label: Create an avatar
tasks.useWhen: The user wants one compact avatar representation rather than a full recurring character production pack.
tasks.directWhen: The avatar itself is the complete output.
tasks.escalateWhen: A canonical recurring identity is required across a narrative or multi-asset system.

tasks.label: Professional headshot
tasks.useWhen: A supplied person needs a polished professional portrait with identity preserved.
tasks.directWhen: One professional portrait or ordinary variation batch is the complete deliverable.
tasks.escalateWhen: The accepted portrait must feed a separately composed identity campaign or multi-format set.

tasks.label: Plan a comic storyboard
tasks.useWhen: The requested deliverable is a structured comic project manifest with pages, panels, dialogue, style, and continuity decisions.
tasks.directWhen: The manifest is the final requested output.
tasks.escalateWhen: The user also requires canonical identities and rendered pages as separately accepted downstream artifacts. Reclassify the final outcome as a narrative sequence before choosing comic-production.

tasks.label: Render a comic page
tasks.useWhen: An existing comic manifest and accepted identity assets must become one rendered page.
tasks.directWhen: One page is requested and all upstream manifest and identity inputs are already accepted.
tasks.escalateWhen: A story manifest, missing identities, or several continuity-linked pages must first be produced.

tasks.label: Plan a film storyboard
tasks.useWhen: The requested text deliverable is an ordered shot manifest with timing, continuity, source roles, and assembly intent.
tasks.directWhen: The storyboard or shot manifest itself is the final result.
tasks.escalateWhen: The user also requires separately generated shots and an assembled video master. Reclassify the final outcome as a narrative sequence before choosing multi-shot-video.

tasks.label: Generate a single video shot
tasks.useWhen: One self-contained video shot must be generated from text and any supported reference assets.
tasks.directWhen: One shot is the complete result and no separate assembly or continuity-linked shot set is requested.
tasks.escalateWhen: Several shots must share timing or continuity and be assembled into one master. Reclassify the final outcome as a narrative sequence before choosing multi-shot-video.

tasks.label: Animate a source image
tasks.useWhen: A supplied still image must become one short motion clip while its core subject and composition remain recognizable.
tasks.directWhen: One animated clip is the complete requested output.
tasks.escalateWhen: The clip is one continuity-linked shot in a separately assembled multi-shot master. Seed a custom runtime DAG so image animation remains the correct shot owner.

tasks.label: Combine video clips
tasks.useWhen: Several supplied or accepted clips must be assembled into one ordered video result.
tasks.directWhen: All clips are supplied and assembly is the only requested operation.
tasks.escalateWhen: The clips must first be generated from a storyboard or require a separately owned finishing branch.

tasks.label: Edit a social video
tasks.useWhen: Supplied footage must become one platform-ready social edit with intentional pacing and format.
tasks.directWhen: The social edit is the complete result and all source footage exists.
tasks.escalateWhen: Missing source shots must be generated or the edit is one of several separately delivered campaign formats. Seed a custom runtime DAG so the social edit remains the final owner.

tasks.label: Restyle an existing room
tasks.useWhen: A supplied room image must retain its spatial structure while adopting a new interior style.
tasks.directWhen: One room restyle is the complete visual result.
tasks.escalateWhen: Verified measurements, a floor-plan artifact, or a research-backed technical brief must first constrain the restyle. Seed a custom runtime DAG whose final node remains restyle-room.

tasks.label: Visualize a floor plan
tasks.useWhen: Supplied plan geometry or spatial measurements must become a clear floor-plan visualization.
tasks.directWhen: The source geometry is authoritative and one visualization is the final result.
tasks.escalateWhen: Measurements or current technical requirements must be verified before visualization. Seed a custom runtime DAG whose final node remains visualize-floor-plan.

tasks.label: Create a flowchart
tasks.useWhen: A supplied process, decision structure, or system relationship must become an accurate flow diagram.
tasks.directWhen: The process facts are supplied and one flowchart is the complete result.
tasks.escalateWhen: Current evidence must be verified before the diagram structure can be fixed. Seed a custom runtime DAG whose final node remains make-flowchart.

tasks.label: Create a CAD model
tasks.useWhen: Dimensions and geometry must become one machine-readable CAD artifact rather than a purely illustrative image.
tasks.directWhen: The geometry and dimensions are supplied and the CAD artifact is the complete result.
tasks.escalateWhen: External specifications or measurements must be verified before geometry can be modeled. Seed a custom runtime DAG whose final node remains create-cad.

tasks.label: Write a cinematic video prompt
tasks.useWhen: The user wants a production-ready prompt for a cinematic shot and does not request media generation.
tasks.directWhen: The prompt text is the complete deliverable.
tasks.escalateWhen: The request requires a separately accepted multi-shot manifest followed by generated and assembled clips. Reclassify the final outcome as a narrative sequence before choosing multi-shot-video.

tasks.label: Diagnose a failed video prompt
tasks.useWhen: A known video generation attempt and its prompt or terminal error must be analyzed to produce a targeted correction plan.
tasks.directWhen: The diagnosis and revised prompt guidance are the complete result.
tasks.escalateWhen: A new execution is separately requested and depends on the accepted diagnosis; preserve the known run state rather than treating diagnosis as permission to resubmit.

tasks.label: Select a video model
tasks.useWhen: The requested deliverable is a reasoned video-model recommendation against a supplied shot and reference-asset contract.
tasks.directWhen: The recommendation is the complete text deliverable.
tasks.escalateWhen: The user requests separately planned shots and media execution after model selection. Reclassify the final outcome as a narrative sequence before choosing multi-shot-video.

tasks.label: Create or revise a custom Skill
tasks.useWhen: The requested result is a local Skill lifecycle artifact: creation, revision, validation, or request-authorized installation.
tasks.directWhen: One management Skill owns the complete local lifecycle requested by the user.
tasks.escalateWhen: Only when separately requested management artifacts have a real dependency; do not enter creative orchestration simply because the subject is a Skill.

recipes.label: Verified product scene to detail-page set
recipes.useWhen: A product-faithful source asset must be accepted before a separate modular detail-page deliverable is composed; add current channel research only when its evidence is independently required downstream.
recipes.directInsteadWhen: Call product-detail-page directly when supplied product imagery and content are sufficient and that Atom owns the complete requested set; call ai-product directly when the only result is one product scene.

steps.objective: Verify only current channel dimensions, module constraints, and claim rules that materially affect the page set.
steps.condition: Current channel facts must be delivered as an independent evidence artifact and reused downstream.
steps.researchScope: Current primary platform documentation with date and source attached to each execution-changing requirement.

steps.objective: Create the accepted product-faithful hero or scene needed by the detail-page composition.
Compose the requested modular buyer-decision sequence and exports from accepted facts and imagery.

finalAcceptance: Every requested module and export exists at the requested or independently verified channel size.
Product identity, geometry, labels, and supplied factual claims remain faithful.
No unverified claim or stale platform requirement appears in the final set.

recipes.label: Shared brief to parallel campaign formats
recipes.useWhen: A shared campaign system must produce at least two independently usable formats or media types whose specialist Atoms can run in parallel after the brief is fixed.
recipes.directInsteadWhen: Dispatch one specialist Atom directly when only one banner, carousel, deck, or video is requested, or when an end-to-end Atom explicitly owns the exact requested bundle.

steps.objective: Normalize the fixed message hierarchy, approved facts, visual invariants, CTA, and per-channel deliverables into one shared brief.
Produce the requested banner exports while preserving the shared campaign system.
steps.condition: A banner placement is an independently requested deliverable.

steps.objective: Produce the requested social carousel as a coherent channel-specific sequence.
steps.condition: A carousel is an independently requested deliverable.

steps.objective: Produce the requested campaign video using the shared facts, identity, and CTA.
steps.condition: A video is an independently requested deliverable.

steps.objective: Register produced artifacts, intended placements, dimensions, shared facts, and any deliberately omitted branch.

finalAcceptance: Every requested channel deliverable is present and mapped to its placement.
Brand identity, approved facts, message hierarchy, and CTA remain consistent across branches.
Each artifact satisfies its owning Atom's technical output contract.

recipes.label: Story manifest to consistent comic pages
recipes.useWhen: A story must become multiple ordered comic pages with a validated manifest, reusable canonical identities, and page-to-page continuity.
recipes.directInsteadWhen: Call plan-comic-storyboard directly when only a manifest is requested; call render-comic-page directly for one page when the manifest and canonical identities are already supplied and accepted.

steps.objective: Create the validated story, page, panel, dialogue, style, and continuity manifest.
Create only missing canonical character sheets required by the manifest before page rendering.
steps.condition: The manifest references a recurring identity without an accepted canonical asset.

steps.objective: Resolve supplied and newly accepted canonical identities into the single page-rendering identity set.
Render every requested page from the manifest and accepted canonical identities.
steps.repeatFor: each requested page in manifest order

steps.objective: Repair exact dialogue placement on otherwise accepted page art without regenerating accepted identities or compositions.
steps.condition: Exact dialogue is the only failed property on otherwise accepted page art.

finalAcceptance: All requested pages exist in manifest order with correct panels and dialogue.
Recurring identities, wardrobe, props, locations, and carried state remain continuous where the manifest requires them.
No accepted page art or canonical identity was regenerated solely to repair dialogue.

recipes.label: Storyboard to assembled multi-shot video
recipes.useWhen: The result requires multiple separately generated shots with explicit timing or continuity followed by assembly into one master.
recipes.directInsteadWhen: Use an end-to-end Atom such as make-music-video, make-product-commercial, pov-short-film-generator, or suspense-title-sequence-generator when it owns the complete requested film and no separate shot assets or approvals are required; call generate-video directly for one shot.

steps.objective: Create the ordered shot manifest with durations, source roles, continuity invariants, and assembly notes.
Generate each shot as an atomic video result from its manifest entry and bound references.
Assemble accepted shot clips in manifest order with the specified pacing and transitions.
Apply one coherent finishing grade only when the assembled master requires cross-shot color normalization.
steps.condition: Cross-shot color normalization or a named final grade is required.

finalAcceptance: The master contains every requested shot once, in the intended order and duration band.
Declared character, product, environment, motion, and carried-state continuity holds across shot boundaries.
Resolution, aspect ratio, audio behavior, and delivery format match the requested master contract.

recipes.label: Source artwork to localized visual set
recipes.useWhen: Several locales, source assets, or channel formats must preserve one visual system while replacing copy and producing a registered localized set.
recipes.directInsteadWhen: Call translate-image-text directly for one supplied image and one target language when its layout-preserving output is the complete request.

steps.objective: Create the source-copy, locale, format, immutable-element, and overflow-handling matrix before image edits.
Replace source copy with locale-appropriate text while preserving declared visual and brand invariants.
Compose localized variants into the requested carousel or deck when a separate series deliverable is required.
steps.condition: The requested final output is a composed series rather than independent localized source images.

steps.objective: Map each final artifact to source, locale, format, dimensions, and copy revision.

finalAcceptance: Every requested source, locale, and format combination is present and correctly named in the delivery manifest.
Translated copy is complete, readable, locale-appropriate, and mapped to the intended source string.
Declared logos, product identity, imagery, hierarchy, and immutable layout elements remain preserved.

recipes.label: Accepted cutout to composed layout
recipes.useWhen: A transparent subject or product cutout is a separately accepted intermediate artifact that must feed a later poster, banner, carousel, or detail layout.
recipes.directInsteadWhen: Call remove-background directly when the transparent cutout is the final result; dispatch the final layout Atom directly when it accepts the original source and owns background removal within its complete output contract.

steps.objective: Create a clean transparent foreground while preserving the declared subject or product boundary.
Compose the accepted cutout into the requested layout without altering protected foreground details.
Export and register the requested dimensions, file formats, transparency behavior, and source lineage.

finalAcceptance: The cutout edge is clean and transparent where required, with no missing protected subject detail.
The final composition matches the requested hierarchy, dimensions, and format.
The foreground identity, geometry, label copy, and declared colors remain unchanged through composition.

recipes.label: Verified evidence to visual deliverable
recipes.useWhen: Current external facts materially determine the content or structure of a visual explanation, deck, infographic, technical visual, or evidence-backed campaign asset.
recipes.directInsteadWhen: Dispatch the owning visual Atom directly when the user supplies an authoritative, sufficient evidence packet and no current-fact verification is needed; perform research alone when no visual deliverable is requested.

steps.objective: Gather and verify only facts that will appear in or structurally change the requested deliverable.
steps.researchScope: Primary or authoritative sources where available, with claim-level citations, dates, unresolved conflicts, and explicit inference labels.

steps.objective: Map verified claims, citations, uncertainty, hierarchy, and prohibited extrapolations into a production brief.
Produce the requested evidence-backed visual with the narrowest runtime-visible Skill that owns the output format.
Attach the final claim-to-source map and record any visual simplification or labeled inference.

finalAcceptance: Every material factual claim maps to a verified source or is clearly labeled as inference.
The visual structure matches the requested audience, format, and decision goal without distorting the evidence.
Dates, units, comparisons, citations, and known uncertainty are complete and internally consistent.
